_meta.raising_a_ceiling: Shrinking always passes. Raising one means the boot payload grew: justify it in the commit body, and never do it to make a red gate green. RAISED AT v1.173.1, gzip only, 385,000 -> 386,400 (+0.36%), and the arithmetic is the whole justification. MEASURED IN CI (the deploy's own gate, run 33775959154): 385,900 against 385,000 — 216 curated journeys passed and this byte count was the single failure. WHERE THE BYTES WENT, measured by building the SAME source tree at three refs and gzipping neural.js: v1.170.1 153,550 -> dev's v1.172.0 154,176 (+626, dev's own two ships) -> this merge 156,105 (+1,929, the three bottom layers). So the ceiling had ~1,000 of headroom and the feature needed ~1,900: dev spent part of it before this branch merged. WHAT WAS TRIED FIRST, because 'never do it to make a red gate green' is the rule above: two duplication sites were consolidated — one ghost-button factory for the four layer handles, and one check-row builder shared by the questions toggle and the three layer rows — which measured 288 bytes, and the settings rows in FULL are only 438, so no amount of tidying reaches 900. Closing the gap would mean deleting a handle the owner asked for by name (the hand ✕, whose crowding is why the see-more hint was removed in this same ship). Those two refactors are NOT in this commit: the disk was full and the box could not run Playwright, so the code here is byte-for-byte the tree CI validated, and only this number moved. WHAT THE BYTES BUY: the film row, the question card and the hand each collapse from their own handle and stay collapsed across landings, reloads and devices — the owner's 'it should still be collapsed'. THIS IS THE OWNER'S CALL TO REVISIT: the ceilings are targets from Cloudflare Observatory field data (LCP P75 13,764ms), and 1,400 bytes gzip is 0.36% of the first-hand payload. If they would rather stay under 385,000, the 288-byte trim plus dropping the three settings rows (438) gets most of the way and only the hand ✕ would still have to go.
